Claude Elwood Shannon was born on April 30, 1916, in Petoskey, Michigan, and died on February 24, 2001, in Medford, Massachusetts. He was an American mathematician, electrical engineer, and computer scientist known as the 'father of information theory'.

Key contributions to information theory include: 1) Founding the field of information theory through his landmark 1948 paper, 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication'. 2) Introducing the concept of the bit (binary digit) as the fundamental unit of information. 3) Defining core concepts such as entropy (quantifying uncertainty or information content), channel capacity, and the noisy-channel coding theorem.
